old: A 1971 10 sentimos from Philippines. Portrait Francisco Baltazar (Balagtas) left, SAMPUNG SENTIMOS, large 10, arms and date on the reverse. Struck in aluminum.
new: A 1971 10 sentimos from Philippines. Portrait Francisco Baltazar (Balagtas) left, SAMPUNG SENTIMOS, large 10, arms and date on the reverse. Struck in nickel-brass.
source: Record PH.KM.198 composition 'nickel brass (Cu 70 / Zn 18 / Ni 12)'; Numista N#3752 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces3752.html): 10 sentimos 1967-1974, KM# 198, nickel brass 70/18/12, 2 g. The story said 'Struck in aluminum', which contradicts both. Only the metal was changed.

old: A 1967 20 cents from Singapore. Value side rice stalks, large 20, CENTS, 1967, SINGAPORE, national arms and lion-fish on the obverse. Struck in cupronickel.
new: A 1967 20 cents from Singapore. Value side two stalks of rice, large 20, CENTS, 1967, SINGAPORE; the other side shows a swordfish against wavy lines for water. Struck in copper-nickel.
source: Numista N#975 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces975.html): Singapore 20 cents 1967-1985 (KM# 4): obverse 'Denomination flanked by two stalks of paddy, date above'; reverse 'Swordfish (Xiphias gladius) facing right against a wavy line background symbolising water'; engraver Stuart Devlin; copper-nickel 75/25. The story said the other side shows the national arms and a lion-fish; there are no arms on this coin and the lionfish is the 50-cent design. 'cupronickel' written as copper-nickel.

old: A 1984 1 dinar from Yugoslavia. The obverse shows SFRY arms (torch and wheat); the reverse shows big 1; bilingual ДИНАР / DINAR legend, date, beaded rim. Struck in brass.
new: A 1984 1 dinar from Yugoslavia. The obverse shows SFRY arms (torch and wheat); the reverse shows big 1; bilingual ДИНАР / DINAR legend, date, beaded rim. Struck in nickel-brass.
source: Numista N#2417 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces2417.html): Yugoslavia 1 dinar, KM# 86, nickel brass (75% Cu, 21% Zn, 4% Ni), 1984 row 172 185 000. The story said 'Struck in brass', copied from the record (YU.KM.86 composition 'brass'), which is corrected to nickel brass in the pending sweep file changes_grok-bot_20261008-0035.jsonl (not merged yet). Only the metal was changed.

old: A 1962 20 centavos from Cuba. The reverse shows large 20 with the date; arms side REPUBLICA DE CUBA, Escudo (key, stripes, palm), oak and laurel, Phrygian-cap star, VEINTE CENTAVOS. Struck in cupronickel.
new: A 1962 20 centavos from Cuba. The reverse shows a portrait of José Martí with the date; arms side REPUBLICA DE CUBA, Escudo (key, stripes, palm), oak and laurel, Phrygian-cap star, VEINTE CENTAVOS. Struck in cupronickel.
source: Numista N#1055 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces1055.html): Cuba 20 centavos 'Martí' 1962-1968, KM# 31, Y# 25, Schön# 29, copper-nickel 75/25, 1962 row 83 860 000; the reverse is the portrait of José Martí with the date. The story said the reverse shows a large 20 with the date. Only the reverse description was changed; the arms side (the photographed side, C252_obv.webp) was left as written.

old: A 1993 10 cents from Jamaica. Arms, crocodile crest, Taino supporters, pineapple cross, OUT OF MANY, ONE PEOPLE, JAMAICA, TEN CENTS, 1993. Struck in cupronickel.
new: A 1993 10 cents from Jamaica. Arms, crocodile crest, Taino supporters, pineapple cross, OUT OF MANY, ONE PEOPLE, JAMAICA, TEN CENTS, 1993. Struck in nickel-plated steel.
source: Numista N#2617 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces2617.html): Jamaica 10 cents large type, KM# 146.1, nickel plated steel, 5.68 g, 23.5 mm; lettering JAMAICA OUT OF MANY, ONE PEOPLE TEN CENTS 1993. The story said cupronickel, copied from the record (JM.KM.146 'cupronickel'), which is corrected to nickel plated steel (and KM 146.1) in the pending sweep file changes_grok-bot_20261008-0002.jsonl. Only the metal was changed.

old: A 1931 3 kopecks from USSR. The obverse shows USSR arms hammer and sickle; the reverse shows large 3; КОПЕЙКИ, wheat ears, 1931. Struck in aluminum-bronze or brass.
new: A 1931 3 kopecks from USSR. The obverse shows USSR arms hammer and sickle; the reverse shows large 3; КОПЕЙКИ, wheat ears, 1931. Struck in aluminium-bronze.
source: Numista N#4042 (https://en.numista.com/catalogue/pieces4042.html): USSR 3 kopecks 1926-1937, Y# 93, aluminium bronze (95% Cu, 5% Al); record SU.Y.93 'aluminum-bronze (Cu 95, Al 5)'. The story said 'aluminum-bronze or brass'; this type was not struck in brass. Only the metal was changed.
